subject: Sales discovery: multilingual model fit & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@globex.de>, Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@aurelia.jp>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Sales discovery: multilingual model fit & next steps

Hi Anna and Kenji —

Thanks again for a great discussion earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

- Key goals you shared: improved customer-facing summarization in DE/FR for EU stores, and accurate account verification & localized responses in JA/KO for APAC operations.
- Success metrics you care about: intent accuracy >= 92% for German/French, hallucination reduction for financial entities under 1%, and latency < 350ms 95th pct for inference in your EU region.
- Privacy/hosting constraint: EU PII must remain in-county for EU pilot; APAC pilot can run in our dedicated region.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share an initial recommended model shortlist and a small localized prompt set we can use for a rapid eval (attached: postcall_notes.pdf).
2) Neha will run an evaluation harness across German, French, Japanese, and Korean with our standard quality and safety checks.
3) If the basic fit looks good, we’ll schedule a 60-min eval review next week to walk benchmarks and iterate on prompts.

Ask: Anna/Kenji — can you confirm which specific DE/FR locales (de-DE vs de-AT, fr-FR vs fr-BE) and whether you have any in-house evaluation data we can reuse? Also let me know any additional compliance constraints (e.g., deletion policy timelines).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the model shortlist and Drive folder with prompt sets & benchmark links.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: postcall_notes.pdf (summary of call notes, action items)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@globex.de>, Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@aurelia.jp>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 01:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sales discovery: multilingual model fit & next steps

Anna — thanks, that’s very helpful. Quick update with concrete artifacts so we can kick off the evals. Links and short guidance below.

Model shortlist (recommended starting point):
- redwood-rlhf-small-multilang: lowest latency, good for short responses and routing / intent tasks.
- redwood-encoder-xl-quant (8-bit): stronger for document understanding and entity extraction in FR/DE; shows lower hallucination on our document benchmarks.
- redwood-instruct-large: best on open-generation quality (JA/KO), but consider quantized variant for cost.

What we’ll evaluate: precision/recall (intent/entity), hallucination rate (entity misattribution), response appropriateness (locale formality), latency distribution, and token cost.

Artifacts shared:
- Localized prompt set (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_localized-evals (includes prompt templates per locale and expected output examples).
- Benchmarks report (public): https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/reports/multilingual-2027-q2 — includes DE/FR/JA/KO slices and methodology.
- Attached prompt CSV: localized_prompt_set_v1.csv (small seed prompts + labels).

Privacy note: For EU PII residency, we can provision a private tenant in our EU region and turn off message-level logging; we will provide a short runbook for on-request deletions. I’ve flagged this to our privacy team and will include the runbook in the eval folder.

Next operational asks for your teams:
1) Anna — please share the anonymized 600 records and the hallucination entity list (SFTP link or Drive).
2) Kenji — confirm JA/KO priority (account verification vs free-text responses) so we can tailor prompts.

Neha/Rishi — cc’d — can you pick this up and run an initial 1k-sample eval across the 4 locales (split by locale roughly equal), and include the following in the deliverable: per-locale confusion matrices, 10 annotated hallucination examples per locale, suggested prompt edits, and a recommendation for model variant to pilot? Target EOW (2027-05-12).

I’ll schedule a 60-min review the week of 2027-05-16 after we have initial numbers.

Thanks — Marissa

Attachment: localized_prompt_set_v1.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: run multilingual evals (DE/FR/JA/KO) — scope and checklist

Neha / Rishi — forwarding the thread with the ask from Globex/Aurelia. Please treat this as priority for the week. Scope + checklist below (copy into the eval ticket):

Scope:
- 1k-sample mix: 250 DE (de-DE), 250 FR (fr-FR), 250 JA (ja-JP), 250 KO (ko-KR). Use the anonymized customer messages Anna will provide when available; otherwise use our synthetic mixes with edge-case entities.
- Models: redwood-rlhf-small-multilang, redwood-encoder-xl-quant, redwood-instruct-large (quant variant).

Checklist / metrics:
- Precision/recall for intent classification and entity extraction per locale.
- Hallucination rate: measured as % of responses containing a fabricated entity when truth set indicates none.
- Localized fluency/formality check: annotate 50 samples per locale for tone appropriateness.
- Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) running from EU and APAC regions (simulate network).
- Token cost estimate per 1k requests for each model variant.
- Stability/regression: run the prompt set against last month’s baseline (multilingual-2027-q1) and surface any regressions >5% in fidelity.

Deliverable: Google Drive folder with CSVs, annotated examples, confusion matrices images, short slide deck (3 slides) with recommended pilot model and next steps. Target due date: 2027-05-12 EOD.

Risks / notes:
- DE/FR entity tokenization sometimes drives higher hallucination on quantized encoders; watch for token-splitting artifacts.
- For JA/KO, ensure byte-pair tokenization differences don’t bias entity extraction metrics — add a tokenization parity check.

If you hit any blockers on data access or compute quotas, escalate to me and I’ll loop in infra.

Thanks — Marissa
